paragraphs.text: Here is a brief description of some rental property agencies to choose from
paragraphs.translation: 以下是一些可供选择的租赁房产机构的简要介绍。

paragraphs.text: A Aynho Properties
paragraphs.translation: A 艾恩霍物业公司

paragraphs.text: with over 50 years experience, we offer a comprehensive sales and lettings service. Our firm has been based in Shipton Street since its foundation and so we have a thorough knowledge of the surrounding neighbourhood. Our staff make every effort to match clients’ needs to an appropriate property, whether you are looking to rent an apartment, a bungalow or a house.
paragraphs.translation:
凭借超过50年的经验，我们提供全面的销售和租赁服务。
自成立以来，我们公司一直位于希普顿街，因此我们对周边社区有着深入的了解。
我们的员工尽一切努力将客户的需求与合适的房产匹配，无论你是想租公寓、平房还是独栋房屋。

paragraphs.text: B Danesdale Agency
paragraphs.translation: B 丹斯代尔中介

paragraphs.text: As soon as you walk in our door, we will make every effort to find the right flat for you to rent. Everything we do is based on good practice - you supply written references and pay the rent on time, and in return we'll visit the property every four months to ensure it is maintained and that any necessary repairs are done.
paragraphs.translation:
一旦您踏入我们的门口，我们将竭尽全力为您找到合适的公寓出租。
我们所做的一切都基于良好实践——您提供书面推荐信并按时支付租金，作为回报，我们每四个月会探访房产一次，以确保其得到维护并完成任何必要的维修。

paragraphs.text: C Jakesford Properties
paragraphs.translation: C 杰克斯福德房产公司

paragraphs.text: As a family-run business with over 20 years' experience in the property market, we pride ourselves on treating every client with kindness and consideration. The landlords on our books have been selected with great care so that you can be sure they will look after your interests. Thousands of customers from allover the world have written to us to express their appreciation for the service we have offered them.
paragraphs.translation:
作为一家在房产市场拥有超过20年经验的家族企业，
我们以友善和体贴地对待每一位客户而自豪。
我们名册上的房东都经过精心挑选，因此您可以确保他们会维护您的利益。

paragraphs.text: D Kasama Letting
paragraphs.translation: D 卡萨马租赁公司

paragraphs.text: our highly experienced team works hard to provide peace of mind for both tenants and landlords. James Kettering, our customer liaison officer, is always at the end of the phone to answer any queries you may have. We also have an administration officer, who deals with contracts, rents and personal queries.
paragraphs.translation:
我们经验丰富的团队努力为租户和房东双方提供安心服务。
我们的客户联络官James Kettering随时接听电话，解答您可能提出的任何疑问。
我们还有一位行政官员，负责处理合同、租金和个人咨询。

paragraphs.text: E Leftfield Letting
paragraphs.translation: E 莱菲尔德租赁公司

paragraphs.text: While the main objective of some letting agents is to get as much money as possible for their properties, we aim to secure a fair deal for tenants and a trouble-free service for landlords. We use modern marketing techniques that include price comparisons for similar properties with other agencies in the area so that you can make a fully informed decision.
paragraphs.translation:
尽管一些租赁中介的主要目标是尽可能从房产中获取更多收益，但我们致力于为租客争取公平的交易，并为房东提供无忧的服务。
我们采用现代营销技巧，包括与地区内其他中介进行同类房产的价格比较，以便您能做出充分知情的决定。

paragraphs.text: Cycle lights
paragraphs.translation: 自行车灯

paragraphs.text: What are the legal requirements?
paragraphs.translation:
法律要求有哪些？
法律要求是什么？

paragraphs.text: A

You must have approved front and rear lights that are lit, clean and working properly when cycling between sunset and sunrise. It's no defence to say that it was past sunset but not yet dark. The legal lighting obligations for cyclists are determined by sunset and sunrise times - not the 'hours of darkness', which start 30 minutes after the former, end 30 minutes before the latter and dictate when motorists must switch from sidelights to headlights.
paragraphs.translation:
在日落至日出期间骑自行车时，你必须拥有经批准的前后灯，这些灯需亮着、干净且正常工作。
以“已过日落但天还未黑”为由并不能作为辩解。
自行车骑手的法定照明义务由日落和日出时间决定，而非“黑暗时段”——后者从日落30分钟后开始，到日出30分钟前结束，并规定机动车驾驶员必须何时从侧灯切换至前照灯。

paragraphs.text: B

Cycling UK's guide to cycling regulations explains the Road Vehicles Lighting Regulations in detail, but in summary you need a white light at the front and a red light at the rear, visible from the front and rear respectively and fixed to your bike. A light obscured by a saddlebag isn't legal and neither is a torch on your head, though there's nothing to stop you using a head-torch as an additional light.
paragraphs.translation:
英国自行车协会的骑行法规指南详细解释了《道路车辆照明条例》，但简而言之，你需要在自行车前部安装一个白色灯，后部安装一个红色灯，这些灯应分别从前后可见，并固定在自行车上。
被鞍包遮挡的灯是不合法的，戴在头上的手电筒也不合法，不过这并不妨碍你使用头灯作为附加照明。

paragraphs.text: C

The regulations also now allow flashing lights, provided they flash between 60 and 240 times per minute. The legal requirements for reflectors include a red rear reflector and four amber pedal reflectors, one at the front and rear of each pedal. Common sense might suggest that a reflective heel strip or ankle band could replace an amber pedal reflector, but unfortunately, these do not meet the legal requirements. This is an annoying problem for riders who use bikes where the feet are attached to the pedals and cannot slip. These pedals are not designed with enough space to accommodate reflectors and make this an area of legislation in need of change.
paragraphs.translation:
现行法规也允许使用闪烁灯，前提是其闪烁频率在每分钟60至240次之间。
对于反光装置的法律要求包括：一个红色后反光器和四个琥珀色踏板反光器，每个踏板的前后各一个。
常识可能认为反光鞋跟条或脚踝带可以替代琥珀色踏板反光器，但不幸的是，这些并不符合法律规定。
这对于那些使用脚部固定在踏板上且无法滑脱的自行车的骑行者来说是个令人烦恼的问题。
这些踏板的设计没有为安装反光器留出足够空间，从而使这一立法领域亟待修订。

paragraphs.text: D

Unlike with other vehicles, lights are not a legal requirement for cyclists when there is seriously reduced visibility during the daytime, although we wouldn't recommend cycling through dense fog without lighting up.
paragraphs.translation: 与其他车辆不同，在白天能见度严重降低的情况下，法律并不要求骑自行车的人必须开灯，尽管我们不建议在没有照明的情况下穿越浓雾骑行。

sentence_translations.sentence: While the main objective of some letting agents is to get as much money as possible for their properties, we aim to secure a fair deal for tenants and a trouble-free service for landlords.

sentence_translations.sentence: Cycle lights
sentence_translations.translation: 自行车灯

sentence_translations.sentence: What are the legal requirements?
sentence_translations.translation: 法律要求有哪些？

sentence_translations.sentence: Want to rent a property?
sentence_translations.translation: 想要租赁一处房产吗？

sentence_translations.sentence: You must have approved front and rear lights that are lit, clean and working properly when cycling between sunset and sunrise.
sentence_translations.translation: 在日落至日出期间骑自行车时，你必须拥有经批准的前后灯，这些灯需亮着、干净且正常工作。

sentence_translations.sentence: It's no defence to say that it was past sunset but not yet dark.
sentence_translations.translation: 以“已过日落但天还未黑”为由并不能作为辩解。

sentence_translations.sentence: The legal lighting obligations for cyclists are determined by sunset and sunrise times - not the 'hours of darkness', which start 30 minutes after the former, end 30 minutes before the latter and dictate when motorists must switch from sidelights to headlights.
sentence_translations.translation: 自行车骑手的法定照明义务由日落和日出时间决定，而非“黑暗时段”——后者从日落30分钟后开始，到日出30分钟前结束，并规定机动车驾驶员必须何时从侧灯切换至前照灯。

sentence_translations.sentence: Cycling UK's guide to cycling regulations explains the Road Vehicles Lighting Regulations in detail, but in summary you need a white light at the front and a red light at the rear, visible from the front and rear respectively and fixed to your bike.
sentence_translations.translation: 英国自行车协会的骑行法规指南详细解释了《道路车辆照明条例》，但简而言之，你需要在自行车前部安装一个白色灯，后部安装一个红色灯，这些灯应分别从前后可见，并固定在自行车上。

sentence_translations.sentence: A light obscured by a saddlebag isn't legal and neither is a torch on your head, though there's nothing to stop you using a head-torch as an additional light.
sentence_translations.translation: 被鞍包遮挡的灯是不合法的，戴在头上的手电筒也不合法，不过这并不妨碍你使用头灯作为附加照明。

sentence_translations.sentence: Cycle lights
sentence_translations.translation: 自行车灯

sentence_translations.sentence: What are the legal requirements?
sentence_translations.translation: 法律要求是什么？

sentence_translations.sentence: The regulations also now allow flashing lights, provided they flash between 60 and 240 times per minute.
sentence_translations.translation: 现行法规也允许使用闪烁灯，前提是其闪烁频率在每分钟60至240次之间。

sentence_translations.sentence: The legal requirements for reflectors include a red rear reflector and four amber pedal reflectors, one at the front and rear of each pedal.
sentence_translations.translation: 对于反光装置的法律要求包括：一个红色后反光器和四个琥珀色踏板反光器，每个踏板的前后各一个。

sentence_translations.sentence: Common sense might suggest that a reflective heel strip or ankle band could replace an amber pedal reflector, but unfortunately, these do not meet the legal requirements.
sentence_translations.translation: 常识可能认为反光鞋跟条或脚踝带可以替代琥珀色踏板反光器，但不幸的是，这些并不符合法律规定。

sentence_translations.sentence: This is an annoying problem for riders who use bikes where the feet are attached to the pedals and cannot slip.
sentence_translations.translation: 这对于那些使用脚部固定在踏板上且无法滑脱的自行车的骑行者来说是个令人烦恼的问题。

sentence_translations.sentence: These pedals are not designed with enough space to accommodate reflectors and make this an area of legislation in need of change.
sentence_translations.translation: 这些踏板的设计没有为安装反光器留出足够空间，从而使这一立法领域亟待修订。

sentence_translations.sentence: Unlike with other vehicles, lights are not a legal requirement for cyclists when there is seriously reduced visibility during the daytime, although we wouldn't recommend cycling through dense fog without lighting up.
sentence_translations.translation: 与其他车辆不同，在白天能见度严重降低的情况下，法律并不要求骑自行车的人必须开灯，尽管我们不建议在没有照明的情况下穿越浓雾骑行。

parts.title: Passage 2
parts.article_title: Maintaining a safe environment for employees working on computers

paragraphs.text: Under health and safety law, you must ensure that the working environment meets certain minimum requirements
paragraphs.translation:
根据健康与安全法律，你必须确保工作环境满足某些最低要求。
工作环境

paragraphs.text: Workstation furniture
paragraphs.translation: 工作站家具

paragraphs.text: The work desk or work surface should be big enough to allow the user to arrange the screen, keyboard and documents, etc. in a flexible way. It should be stable and positioned so that it's comfortable when an employee uses a document holder, but also big enough to let the user work comfortably and to alter their position.
paragraphs.translation:
办公桌或工作台应足够宽敞，以便使用者能够灵活地布置屏幕、键盘和文件等物品。
它应保持稳定且摆放得当，使员工在使用文件架时感到舒适，同时也应足够大，以便使用者能舒适地工作并能调整自己的姿势。

paragraphs.text: The working environment
paragraphs.translation: 工作环境

paragraphs.text: You need to assess noise levels. The equipment shouldn't be so noisy that it distracts the user. If you can't use quieter equipment, consider soundproofing or moving the equipment. You could use partitions between noisy equipment and the rest of the workstation as an alternative.
paragraphs.translation:
你需要评估噪音水平。
设备不应过于嘈杂以免分散用户的注意力。
如果你无法使用更安静的设备，可以考虑隔音或移动设备。
作为一种替代方案，你可以在嘈杂设备与工作站其他区域之间使用隔断。

paragraphs.text: Lighting is also an important consideration. Surrounding windows must have curtains or blinds which users can adjust to prevent reflected glare. If needed, provide users with lighting appropriate to their tasks and particular workstation. Users should have control over their lighting to prevent reflected glare.
paragraphs.translation:
照明也是一个重要的考虑因素。
周围的窗户必须配备用户可调节的窗帘或百叶窗，以防止反射眩光。
如有需要，应为用户提供适合其工作任务和特定工作站的照明。
用户应能控制自己的照明，以防止反射眩光。

paragraphs.text: Temperature-wise, the equipment should not give out so much heat that the user becomes uncomfortable, so monitor this. It's also important that you maintain ventilation, and you control humidity so that it is at a level which keeps the user comfortable.
paragraphs.translation:
在温度方面，设备不应散发出过多热量导致使用者感到不适，因此需对此加以监控。
保持通风以及控制湿度至令使用者舒适的水平也同样重要。

paragraphs.text: Task design and rest breaks
paragraphs.translation: 任务设计与休息间隔

paragraphs.text: Good design of the task can be as important as the right choice of furniture and equipment. Whenever possible you should design jobs so that employees have a mix of activities and some control over which tasks they perform and when. You should match staffing levels to workload so that individuals are neither overworked nor underworked and give employees some say in the way work is carried out and the planning that goes into it.
paragraphs.translation:
任务的良好设计与正确选择家具和设备同样重要。
只要有可能，你就应该设计工作，使员工能够进行多样化的活动，并对他们执行哪些任务以及何时执行拥有一定的控制权。
你应该使人员配置水平与工作量相匹配，以确保员工既不过度劳累也不过于清闲，并让员工在工作的执行方式和相关规划中有一定的发言权。

paragraphs.text: An employee's need for rest breaks will vary depending on the type of work they are doing and how intensely they are working. As a general rule, however, short, frequent breaks are better than longer, less frequent ones. A 5-10-minute break after 50-60 minutes' work is better than a 15-20-minute break after two hours. The employee should, at times, have a choice over when to take breaks and they should be encouraged to do non-work activities during their break, ideally away from the workstation.
paragraphs.translation:
员工对休息间隔的需求会因所从事工作的类型和工作强度而有所不同。
然而，一般来说，短暂而频繁的休息优于较长但不频繁的休息。
工作50-60分钟后休息5-10分钟，优于工作两小时后休息15-20分钟。
员工有时应有权选择何时休息，并应鼓励他们在休息期间进行非工作活动，最好远离工作台。

paragraphs.text: Using portable ladders
paragraphs.translation: 使用便携式梯子

paragraphs.text: Workers use portable ladders for a variety of jobs outside, such as first- and second-floor window cleaning and building repairs
paragraphs.translation: 工人在户外使用便携式梯子从事多种工作，例如一楼和二楼的窗户清洁以及建筑维修。

paragraphs.text: A

Employers need to oversee all ladders that are owned by their company. Detailed visual inspections should be carried out on a regular basis, and they should have an up-to-date record of these. Before starting a job, employers are also responsible for ensuring any ladder is the right length to meet the needs of the task; reaching out from the very top of a ladder is highly dangerous. Once you get a ladder, you, as user of the ladder, should conduct a pre-use check each working day. Conducting pre-use checks should have been part of your training and should be done in accordance with the manufacturer's guidelines. When doing a check, it is important to focus on the steps and make sure they are not loose as this could cause an accident. Similarly, a cracked joint in the ladder could cause it to fail.
paragraphs.translation:
雇主需要监管公司拥有的所有梯子。
应定期进行详细的目视检查，并保持对这些检查的最新记录。
在开始工作前，雇主还有责任确保任何梯子的长度符合任务需求；从梯子最顶端伸手够物是极其危险的。
拿到梯子后，作为使用者，你应该在每个工作日进行使用前检查。
进行使用前检查本应是培训的一部分，并且应按照制造商的指导说明进行。
进行检查时，重点应放在梯级上，确保它们不松动，因为这可能导致事故。
同样，梯子上的裂缝接头可能导致梯子失效。

paragraphs.text: B

Almost all falls from ladders happen because the ladder moves unexpectedly. The key factor in preventing falls from ladders is to ensure your ladder is stable whilst being used. First, make sure that you choose level ground on which to set up your ladder. There are specially designed tools you can use to ensure this - don't just use a piece of wood. Second, check the ground surface is dirt-free and solid, so the feet can grip and the ladder doesn't sink.
paragraphs.translation:
几乎所有的梯子坠落事故都是由于梯子意外移动而发生的。
预防梯子坠落的关键因素是确保梯子在使用过程中保持稳定。
首先，确保你选择平整的地面来放置梯子。
有专门设计的工具可以用来确保这一点——不要仅仅使用一块木头。
其次，检查地面是否无污垢且坚实，这样梯脚能够抓牢，梯子不会下陷。

paragraphs.text: C

Before you go up your ladder, look at the surrounding environment. Make sure the ladder cannot be struck by vehicles. If necessary, safeguard the area by placing red and white cones around it. Ensure it will not be pushed over by other hazards such as opening doors. Doors and windows may need to be secured where possible.
paragraphs.translation:
在爬上梯子之前，请先观察周围环境。
确保梯子不会受到车辆的撞击。
如有必要，通过在周围放置红白锥形路障来保护该区域。
确保它不会被其他危险因素（如开门）推倒。
在可能的情况下，可能需要将门窗固定好。

paragraphs.text: Finally, think about the hazards to the general public and make sure they cannot walk underneath it or get too near to it. A 'danger' sign at the base is often the best way of doing this.
paragraphs.translation:
最后，要考虑对公众造成的危险，确保他们无法从梯子下方走过或过于靠近梯子。
在梯子底部放置‘危险’标志通常是做到这一点的最佳方式。

paragraphs.text: D

To secure the ladder, tie it to a suitable point, such as a window or railing, making sure both sides are attached. Where this is not practical, secure it to the wall near the base of the ladder with ties; avoid using blocks to wedge the ladder in place as they can easily move.
paragraphs.translation:
为了固定梯子，应将其系在合适的位置，例如窗户或栏杆上，并确保两侧都已绑好。
如果这种方法不可行，则用绳索将梯子固定在靠近基部的墙壁上；避免使用木块楔入梯子来固定位置，因为它们很容易移动。

parts.source_article_title: Maintaining a safe environment for employees working on computers

sentence_translations.sentence: Under health and safety law, you must ensure that the working environment meets certain minimum requirements
sentence_translations.translation: 根据健康与安全法律，你必须确保工作环境满足某些最低要求。

sentence_translations.sentence: Workstation furniture
sentence_translations.translation: 工作站家具

sentence_translations.sentence: The work desk or work surface should be big enough to allow the user to arrange the screen, keyboard and documents, etc. in a flexible way.
sentence_translations.translation: 办公桌或工作台应足够宽敞，以便使用者能够灵活地布置屏幕、键盘和文件等物品。

sentence_translations.sentence: It should be stable and positioned so that it's comfortable when an employee uses a document holder, but also big enough to let the user work comfortably and to alter their position.
sentence_translations.translation: 它应保持稳定且摆放得当，使员工在使用文件架时感到舒适，同时也应足够大，以便使用者能舒适地工作并能调整自己的姿势。

sentence_translations.sentence: The working environment
sentence_translations.translation: 工作环境

sentence_translations.sentence: You need to assess noise levels.
sentence_translations.translation: 你需要评估噪音水平。

sentence_translations.sentence: The equipment shouldn't be so noisy that it distracts the user.
sentence_translations.translation: 设备不应过于嘈杂以免分散用户的注意力。

sentence_translations.sentence: If you can't use quieter equipment, consider soundproofing or moving the equipment.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果你无法使用更安静的设备，可以考虑隔音或移动设备。

sentence_translations.sentence: You could use partitions between noisy equipment and the rest of the workstation as an alternative.
sentence_translations.translation: 作为一种替代方案，你可以在嘈杂设备与工作站其他区域之间使用隔断。

sentence_translations.sentence: Lighting is also an important consideration.
sentence_translations.translation: 照明也是一个重要的考虑因素。

sentence_translations.sentence: Surrounding windows must have curtains or blinds which users can adjust to prevent reflected glare.
sentence_translations.translation: 周围的窗户必须配备用户可调节的窗帘或百叶窗，以防止反射眩光。

sentence_translations.sentence: If needed, provide users with lighting appropriate to their tasks and particular workstation.
sentence_translations.translation: 如有需要，应为用户提供适合其工作任务和特定工作站的照明。

sentence_translations.sentence: Users should have control over their lighting to prevent reflected glare.
sentence_translations.translation: 用户应能控制自己的照明，以防止反射眩光。

sentence_translations.sentence: Temperature-wise, the equipment should not give out so much heat that the user becomes uncomfortable, so monitor this.
sentence_translations.translation: 在温度方面，设备不应散发出过多热量导致使用者感到不适，因此需对此加以监控。

sentence_translations.sentence: It's also important that you maintain ventilation, and you control humidity so that it is at a level which keeps the user comfortable.
sentence_translations.translation: 保持通风以及控制湿度至令使用者舒适的水平也同样重要。

sentence_translations.sentence: Task design and rest breaks
sentence_translations.translation: 任务设计与休息间隔

sentence_translations.sentence: Good design of the task can be as important as the right choice of furniture and equipment.
sentence_translations.translation: 任务的良好设计与正确选择家具和设备同样重要。

sentence_translations.sentence: Whenever possible you should design jobs so that employees have a mix of activities and some control over which tasks they perform and when.
sentence_translations.translation: 只要有可能，你就应该设计工作，使员工能够进行多样化的活动，并对他们执行哪些任务以及何时执行拥有一定的控制权。

sentence_translations.sentence: You should match staffing levels to workload so that individuals are neither overworked nor underworked and give employees some say in the way work is carried out and the planning that goes into it.
sentence_translations.translation: 你应该使人员配置水平与工作量相匹配，以确保员工既不过度劳累也不过于清闲，并让员工在工作的执行方式和相关规划中有一定的发言权。

sentence_translations.sentence: An employee's need for rest breaks will vary depending on the type of work they are doing and how intensely they are working.
sentence_translations.translation: 员工对休息间隔的需求会因所从事工作的类型和工作强度而有所不同。

sentence_translations.sentence: As a general rule, however, short, frequent breaks are better than longer, less frequent ones.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，一般来说，短暂而频繁的休息优于较长但不频繁的休息。

sentence_translations.sentence: A 5-10-minute break after 50-60 minutes' work is better than a 15-20-minute break after two hours.
sentence_translations.translation: 工作50-60分钟后休息5-10分钟，优于工作两小时后休息15-20分钟。

sentence_translations.sentence: The employee should, at times, have a choice over when to take breaks and they should be encouraged to do non-work activities during their break, ideally away from the workstation.
sentence_translations.translation: 员工有时应有权选择何时休息，并应鼓励他们在休息期间进行非工作活动，最好远离工作台。

sentence_translations.sentence: Using portable ladders
sentence_translations.translation: 使用便携式梯子

sentence_translations.sentence: Workers use portable ladders for a variety of jobs outside, such as first- and second-floor window cleaning and building repairs
sentence_translations.translation: 工人在户外使用便携式梯子从事多种工作，例如一楼和二楼的窗户清洁以及建筑维修。

sentence_translations.sentence: Employers need to oversee all ladders that are owned by their company.
sentence_translations.translation: 雇主需要监管公司拥有的所有梯子。

sentence_translations.sentence: Detailed visual inspections should be carried out on a regular basis, and they should have an up-to-date record of these.
sentence_translations.translation: 应定期进行详细的目视检查，并保持对这些检查的最新记录。

sentence_translations.sentence: Before starting a job, employers are also responsible for ensuring any ladder is the right length to meet the needs of the task; reaching out from the very top of a ladder is highly dangerous.
sentence_translations.translation: 在开始工作前，雇主还有责任确保任何梯子的长度符合任务需求；从梯子最顶端伸手够物是极其危险的。

sentence_translations.sentence: Once you get a ladder, you, as user of the ladder, should conduct a pre-use check each working day.
sentence_translations.translation: 拿到梯子后，作为使用者，你应该在每个工作日进行使用前检查。

sentence_translations.sentence: Conducting pre-use checks should have been part of your training and should be done in accordance with the manufacturer's guidelines.
sentence_translations.translation: 进行使用前检查本应是培训的一部分，并且应按照制造商的指导说明进行。

sentence_translations.sentence: When doing a check, it is important to focus on the steps and make sure they are not loose as this could cause an accident.
sentence_translations.translation: 进行检查时，重点应放在梯级上，确保它们不松动，因为这可能导致事故。

sentence_translations.sentence: Similarly, a cracked joint in the ladder could cause it to fail.
sentence_translations.translation: 同样，梯子上的裂缝接头可能导致梯子失效。

sentence_translations.sentence: Almost all falls from ladders happen because the ladder moves unexpectedly.
sentence_translations.translation: 几乎所有的梯子坠落事故都是由于梯子意外移动而发生的。

sentence_translations.sentence: The key factor in preventing falls from ladders is to ensure your ladder is stable whilst being used.
sentence_translations.translation: 预防梯子坠落的关键因素是确保梯子在使用过程中保持稳定。

sentence_translations.sentence: First, make sure that you choose level ground on which to set up your ladder.
sentence_translations.translation: 首先，确保你选择平整的地面来放置梯子。

sentence_translations.sentence: There are specially designed tools you can use to ensure this - don't just use a piece of wood.
sentence_translations.translation: 有专门设计的工具可以用来确保这一点——不要仅仅使用一块木头。

sentence_translations.sentence: Second, check the ground surface is dirt-free and solid, so the feet can grip and the ladder doesn't sink.
sentence_translations.translation: 其次，检查地面是否无污垢且坚实，这样梯脚能够抓牢，梯子不会下陷。

sentence_translations.sentence: Before you go up your ladder, look at the surrounding environment.
sentence_translations.translation: 在爬上梯子之前，请先观察周围环境。

sentence_translations.sentence: Make sure the ladder cannot be struck by vehicles.
sentence_translations.translation: 确保梯子不会受到车辆的撞击。

sentence_translations.sentence: If necessary, safeguard the area by placing red and white cones around it.
sentence_translations.translation: 如有必要，通过在周围放置红白锥形路障来保护该区域。

sentence_translations.sentence: Ensure it will not be pushed over by other hazards such as opening doors.
sentence_translations.translation: 确保它不会被其他危险因素（如开门）推倒。

sentence_translations.sentence: Doors and windows may need to be secured where possible.
sentence_translations.translation: 在可能的情况下，可能需要将门窗固定好。

sentence_translations.sentence: Finally, think about the hazards to the general public and make sure they cannot walk underneath it or get too near to it.
sentence_translations.translation: 最后，要考虑对公众造成的危险，确保他们无法从梯子下方走过或过于靠近梯子。

sentence_translations.sentence: A 'danger' sign at the base is often the best way of doing this.
sentence_translations.translation: 在梯子底部放置‘危险’标志通常是做到这一点的最佳方式。

sentence_translations.sentence: To secure the ladder, tie it to a suitable point, such as a window or railing, making sure both sides are attached.
sentence_translations.translation: 为了固定梯子，应将其系在合适的位置，例如窗户或栏杆上，并确保两侧都已绑好。

sentence_translations.sentence: Where this is not practical, secure it to the wall near the base of the ladder with ties; avoid using blocks to wedge the ladder in place as they can easily move.
sentence_translations.translation: 如果这种方法不可行，则用绳索将梯子固定在靠近基部的墙壁上；避免使用木块楔入梯子来固定位置，因为它们很容易移动。

parts.title: Passage 3
parts.article_title: The story of the Fosbury Flop

paragraphs.text: A

On October 20,1968, a 21-year-old university student from the USA called Dick Fosbury completely transformed the sport of high jumping with a gold-medal and Olympic-record jump of 2.24 meters at the Mexico City games. Fosbury accomplished this fabulous feat by sailing over the crossbar head first and backward! As colorfully described that day by the Los Angeles Times,"Fosbury goes over the bar like a guy being pushed out of a 30-story window."
paragraphs.translation:
1968年10月20日，一位来自美国的21岁大学生，名叫迪克·福斯伯里，在墨西哥城奥运会上以2.24米的金牌成绩和奥运纪录彻底改变了跳高运动。
福斯伯里通过头先向后飞跃横杆的方式完成了这一惊人壮举。
正如《洛杉矶时报》那天生动描述的：“福斯伯里越过横杆的样子，就像一个人被从30层楼的窗户推出去一样。”

paragraphs.text: B

At first, when asked about how this unorthodox manoeuvre originated, Fosbury would joke with sportswriters, informing some that, because of his university background in physics and engineering, he had initially designed the Flop on paper, and telling others that he had accidentally discovered this technique when he once tripped and fell backward on his take-off. However, in later interviews, Fosbury revealed that the technique actually unfolded over many years and involved countless trials and errors. " It was simply a natural technique that evolved," he said." I never thought about how to change it, and I'm sure my coach was going crazy because it kept evolving. l didn't know anyone else in the world would be able to use it."
paragraphs.translation:
起初，当被问及这种非正统动作是如何起源时，福斯伯里会与体育记者开玩笑，告诉一些人，由于他大学主修物理和工程学，他最初在纸上设计了背越式，而告诉另一些人，他是在一次起跳时绊倒并向后摔倒时偶然发现了这项技术。
然而，在后来的采访中，福斯伯里透露，这项技术实际上是经过多年发展而成的，并涉及无数次的尝试和错误。
“这只是一项自然演变的技术，”他说，“我从未想过如何改变它，而且我确信我的教练快要疯了，因为它不断演变。我不知道世界上还有其他人能够使用它。”

paragraphs.text: C

Fosbury explained that when he first learned to high jump at the age of 10 or 11, he tried jumping with the "scissors" style. He said, " l used that style until l went into high school, where my coach explained that l was never going to get anywhere with that technique. He started me with the 'belly roll' technique.
paragraphs.translation:
福斯贝里解释说，在他10岁或11岁第一次学习跳高时，他曾尝试用“剪式”跳法。
他说：“我一直使用那种风格，直到进入高中，我的教练解释说，用那种技术我永远不会有任何进展。
他让我开始学习‘腹滚式’技术。”

paragraphs.text: However, l was really lousy with that style. l expressed my frustration to coach and he said that if l really wanted, l could still use the 'scissors.
paragraphs.translation:
然而，我运用那种姿势时表现非常糟糕。
我向教练表达了沮丧之情，他说如果我真心愿意，我仍然可以使用‘剪刀式’跳法。

paragraphs.text: So, in his next competition, Fosbury went back to the "scissors" style. He explained: "As the bar was raised each time, l began to lift my hips up and my shoulders went back in reaction to that. At the end of the competition, I had improved my best by 15 cm to 1 m 78 and even placed third! The next two years in high school with my curved approach, l began to lead with my shoulder and eventually was going over head first like today's Floppers."
paragraphs.translation:
所以，在接下来的比赛中，福斯伯里重新使用了“剪刀式”跳法。
他解释说：“每次横杆升高时，我开始抬起臀部，肩膀随之向后仰。
比赛结束时，我的最佳成绩提高了15厘米，达到1米78，甚至获得了第三名！”
在接下来的两年高中生涯中，我采用曲线助跑，开始用肩膀引领，最终像今天的背越式跳高者一样头朝下越过横杆。”

paragraphs.text: D

In this way, the Flop evolved, not from design, but from a trial-and-error process which combined repeated effort with the biomechanics of Fosbury's gangling 1 m 93 physique. Sports Illustrated writer Richard Hoffer wrote: "It was on-site engineering, his body and mind working together, making reflexive adjustments with only one goal, getting over the bar." Hoffer explained that although Fosbury's arms and legs seemed to be all over the place, those movements that served to get him a centimeter higher were retained, while the others were gradually eliminated as the technique evolved.
paragraphs.translation:
就这样，背越式跳高并非源自设计，而是通过反复尝试与错误的过程演变而来，这一过程结合了福斯伯里瘦长身材（身高1米93）的生物力学特性。
《体育画报》撰稿人理查德·霍弗写道：“这是现场工程，他的身心协同工作，进行反射性调整，目标只有一个——越过横杆。”
霍弗解释道，尽管福斯伯里的手臂和腿显得杂乱无章，但那些能让他再高一厘米的动作被保留了下来，而其他动作则随着技术的演变逐渐被淘汰。
就这样，背越式跳高逐渐演变而来，并非出于设计，而是一个反复尝试的过程，将反复的努力与福斯伯里瘦长身材（身高1米93）的生物力学特性结合在一起。
《体育画报》的作者理查德·霍弗写道：“这是一场现场工程，他的身体和心智协同工作，做出本能调整，目标只有一个——过杆。”
霍弗解释说，尽管福斯伯里的手臂和腿似乎显得杂乱无章，但那些能让他再高一厘米的动作被保留下来，而其他动作则随着技术的演变逐渐被淘汰。

paragraphs.text: E

What did Fosbury think of the seeming awkwardness of his Flop?" l believe that the Flop was a natural style," he said,"And l was just the first to find it. I can say that because the Canadian jumper Debbie Brill was a few years younger than l was and also developed the same technique, only a few years after me and without ever having seen me."
paragraphs.translation:
福斯贝里如何看待他那看似笨拙的背越式跳高？
"我认为背越式是一种自然的动作，"他说，"我只是第一个发现它的人。
我可以这么说，因为加拿大跳高选手黛比·布里尔比我年轻几岁，也在几年后独立发展出了同样的技术，而且从未看过我的动作。"

paragraphs.text: A striking coincidence? Yes, indeed. But, perhaps not as striking as the fact that a high school student called Bruce Quande was photographed on May 24,1963 flopping backward over the crossbar. This was the same month that Fosbury recalls having flopped for the first time in the competition when he was at high school!
paragraphs.translation:
一个惊人的巧合吗？
确实是的。
但也许更令人惊讶的是，一名叫布鲁斯·匡德的高中生在1963年5月24日被拍到向后越过横杆。
这正是福斯伯里回忆自己在高中比赛中第一次使用背越式跳高的同一个月！

paragraphs.text: F

But completing the Flop successfully was only half the battle; the return to earth still had to be negotiated. Few would even consider such an experiment knowing they'd have to land on their necks. When Fosbury was jumping in high school, he had to land in pits which were filled with wood chips, sawdust, or sand. On one occasion, Fosbury hit his head on the wooden border of the pit. Another time he landed totally out of the pit, flat on his back, knocking the wind out of him. The next year, Fosbury's high school became the first in the region to install foam rubber in its high jump pit, thereby cushioning the jumper's fall and encouraging the use of the potentially dangerous Flop. The Fosbury Flop and cushioned landing areas thus appear to have co-evolved.
paragraphs.translation:
但是，成功完成背越式跳高只是成功了一半；返回地面这一环节仍需解决。
很少有人会考虑进行这样的尝试，因为他们知道自己将不得不以颈部着地。
当福斯伯里在高中练习跳高时，他不得不落在装满木屑、锯末或沙子的坑里。
有一次，福斯伯里的头撞在了坑的木制边框上。
还有一次，他完全落在了坑外，背部平摔在地上，摔得他喘不过气来。
第二年，福斯伯里的高中成为该地区第一所在跳高坑中安装泡沫橡胶的学校，从而缓冲了跳高者的下落，并鼓励采用这种具有潜在危险的背越式跳法。
因此，福斯伯里背越式和缓冲落地区域似乎是共同演化的。

paragraphs.text: G

Fosbury explains how he came to name the Flop."I'm very proud that l received the naming rights. But the term by which the style is known did not appear overnight. To tell the truth, the first time that I was interviewed and asked 'What do you call this?' l used my engineering analytical side and l referred to it as a 'back layout.'It was not interesting, and the journalist didn't even write it down.l noted this. The next time that l was interviewed, that's when l said: "Well, at home in my town they call it the Fosbury Flop' - and everyone wrote it down.l was the first one to call it that, but it came from a caption on a newspaper photo that said: 'Fosbury flops over bar.' The context was that our town was on a river, very popular for fishing, an hour from the Pacific Ocean. And when you land a fish on the bank, it's flopping. That's the action, and so it's a good description by a journalist, and l remembered it."
paragraphs.translation:
福斯贝里解释了他如何为“背越式跳高”命名。
“我非常自豪我获得了命名权。
但这种姿势所采用的术语并非一夜之间出现的。
说实话，第一次接受采访被问到‘你怎么称呼这个？’时，我运用了自己工程分析的一面，称之为‘背式’。
这并不有趣，记者甚至没有记下来。
我注意到了这一点。
第二次接受采访时，我说：‘嗯，在我家乡小镇，他们称之为“福斯贝里背越式”’——然后每个人都记了下来。
我是第一个这么称呼它的人，但这源自一张报纸照片下的说明文字：‘福斯贝里背越横杆。’
背景是，我们小镇位于一条河边，很适合钓鱼，距离太平洋一小时车程。
当你把鱼甩到岸上时，它会扑腾。
那就是这种动作，所以这真是记者一个好描述，而我记住了它。”

questions.analysis: 题干要求匹配“建议Fosbury改变跳法”的段落。C段提到教练认为他用“scissors”风格“永远不会有所成就”，于是让他改练“belly roll”技术，这正是一次明确的改进建议。因此，段落C最符合题干描述。

parts.source_article_title: The story of the Fosbury Flop

sentence_translations.sentence: On October 20,1968, a 21-year-old university student from the USA called Dick Fosbury completely transformed the sport of high jumping with a gold-medal and Olympic-record jump of 2.24 meters at the Mexico City games.
sentence_translations.translation: 1968年10月20日，一位来自美国的21岁大学生，名叫迪克·福斯伯里，在墨西哥城奥运会上以2.24米的金牌成绩和奥运纪录彻底改变了跳高运动。

sentence_translations.sentence: Fosbury accomplished this fabulous feat by sailing over the crossbar head first and backward!
sentence_translations.translation: 福斯伯里通过头先向后飞跃横杆的方式完成了这一惊人壮举。

sentence_translations.sentence: As colorfully described that day by the Los Angeles Times,"Fosbury goes over the bar like a guy being pushed out of a 30-story window."
sentence_translations.translation: 正如《洛杉矶时报》那天生动描述的：“福斯伯里越过横杆的样子，就像一个人被从30层楼的窗户推出去一样。”

sentence_translations.sentence: At first, when asked about how this unorthodox manoeuvre originated, Fosbury would joke with sportswriters, informing some that, because of his university background in physics and engineering, he had initially designed the Flop on paper, and telling others that he had accidentally discovered this technique when he once tripped and fell backward on his take-off.
sentence_translations.translation: 起初，当被问及这种非正统动作是如何起源时，福斯伯里会与体育记者开玩笑，告诉一些人，由于他大学主修物理和工程学，他最初在纸上设计了背越式，而告诉另一些人，他是在一次起跳时绊倒并向后摔倒时偶然发现了这项技术。

sentence_translations.sentence: However, in later interviews, Fosbury revealed that the technique actually unfolded over many years and involved countless trials and errors.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，在后来的采访中，福斯伯里透露，这项技术实际上是经过多年发展而成的，并涉及无数次的尝试和错误。

sentence_translations.sentence: " It was simply a natural technique that evolved," he said." I never thought about how to change it, and I'm sure my coach was going crazy because it kept evolving. l didn't know anyone else in the world would be able to use it."
sentence_translations.translation: “这只是一项自然演变的技术，”他说，“我从未想过如何改变它，而且我确信我的教练快要疯了，因为它不断演变。我不知道世界上还有其他人能够使用它。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Fosbury explained that when he first learned to high jump at the age of 10 or 11, he tried jumping with the "scissors" style.
sentence_translations.translation: 福斯贝里解释说，在他10岁或11岁第一次学习跳高时，他曾尝试用“剪式”跳法。

sentence_translations.sentence: He said, " l used that style until l went into high school, where my coach explained that l was never going to get anywhere with that technique.
sentence_translations.translation: 他说：“我一直使用那种风格，直到进入高中，我的教练解释说，用那种技术我永远不会有任何进展。

sentence_translations.sentence: He started me with the 'belly roll' technique.
sentence_translations.translation: 他让我开始学习‘腹滚式’技术。”

sentence_translations.sentence: However, l was really lousy with that style.
sentence_translations.translation: 然而，我运用那种姿势时表现非常糟糕。

sentence_translations.sentence: l expressed my frustration to coach and he said that if l really wanted, l could still use the 'scissors.
sentence_translations.translation: 我向教练表达了沮丧之情，他说如果我真心愿意，我仍然可以使用‘剪刀式’跳法。

sentence_translations.sentence: So, in his next competition, Fosbury went back to the "scissors" style.
sentence_translations.translation: 所以，在接下来的比赛中，福斯伯里重新使用了“剪刀式”跳法。

sentence_translations.sentence: He explained: "As the bar was raised each time, l began to lift my hips up and my shoulders went back in reaction to that.
sentence_translations.translation: 他解释说：“每次横杆升高时，我开始抬起臀部，肩膀随之向后仰。

sentence_translations.sentence: At the end of the competition, I had improved my best by 15 cm to 1 m 78 and even placed third!
sentence_translations.translation: 比赛结束时，我的最佳成绩提高了15厘米，达到1米78，甚至获得了第三名！”

sentence_translations.sentence: The next two years in high school with my curved approach, l began to lead with my shoulder and eventually was going over head first like today's Floppers."
sentence_translations.translation: 在接下来的两年高中生涯中，我采用曲线助跑，开始用肩膀引领，最终像今天的背越式跳高者一样头朝下越过横杆。”

sentence_translations.sentence: In this way, the Flop evolved, not from design, but from a trial-and-error process which combined repeated effort with the biomechanics of Fosbury's gangling 1 m 93 physique.
sentence_translations.translation: 就这样，背越式跳高并非源自设计，而是通过反复尝试与错误的过程演变而来，这一过程结合了福斯伯里瘦长身材（身高1米93）的生物力学特性。

sentence_translations.sentence: Sports Illustrated writer Richard Hoffer wrote: "It was on-site engineering, his body and mind working together, making reflexive adjustments with only one goal, getting over the bar."
sentence_translations.translation: 《体育画报》撰稿人理查德·霍弗写道：“这是现场工程，他的身心协同工作，进行反射性调整，目标只有一个——越过横杆。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Hoffer explained that although Fosbury's arms and legs seemed to be all over the place, those movements that served to get him a centimeter higher were retained, while the others were gradually eliminated as the technique evolved.
sentence_translations.translation: 霍弗解释道，尽管福斯伯里的手臂和腿显得杂乱无章，但那些能让他再高一厘米的动作被保留了下来，而其他动作则随着技术的演变逐渐被淘汰。

sentence_translations.sentence: In this way, the Flop evolved, not from design, but from a trial-and-error process which combined repeated effort with the biomechanics of Fosbury's gangling 1 m 93 physique.
sentence_translations.translation: 就这样，背越式跳高逐渐演变而来，并非出于设计，而是一个反复尝试的过程，将反复的努力与福斯伯里瘦长身材（身高1米93）的生物力学特性结合在一起。

sentence_translations.sentence: Sports Illustrated writer Richard Hoffer wrote: "It was on-site engineering, his body and mind working together, making reflexive adjustments with only one goal, getting over the bar."
sentence_translations.translation: 《体育画报》的作者理查德·霍弗写道：“这是一场现场工程，他的身体和心智协同工作，做出本能调整，目标只有一个——过杆。”

sentence_translations.sentence: Hoffer explained that although Fosbury's arms and legs seemed to be all over the place, those movements that served to get him a centimeter higher were retained, while the others were gradually eliminated as the technique evolved.
sentence_translations.translation: 霍弗解释说，尽管福斯伯里的手臂和腿似乎显得杂乱无章，但那些能让他再高一厘米的动作被保留下来，而其他动作则随着技术的演变逐渐被淘汰。

sentence_translations.sentence: What did Fosbury think of the seeming awkwardness of his Flop?
sentence_translations.translation: 福斯贝里如何看待他那看似笨拙的背越式跳高？

sentence_translations.sentence: " l believe that the Flop was a natural style," he said,"And l was just the first to find it.
sentence_translations.translation: "我认为背越式是一种自然的动作，"他说，"我只是第一个发现它的人。

sentence_translations.sentence: I can say that because the Canadian jumper Debbie Brill was a few years younger than l was and also developed the same technique, only a few years after me and without ever having seen me."
sentence_translations.translation: 我可以这么说，因为加拿大跳高选手黛比·布里尔比我年轻几岁，也在几年后独立发展出了同样的技术，而且从未看过我的动作。"

sentence_translations.sentence: A striking coincidence?
sentence_translations.translation: 一个惊人的巧合吗？

sentence_translations.sentence: Yes, indeed.
sentence_translations.translation: 确实是的。

sentence_translations.sentence: But, perhaps not as striking as the fact that a high school student called Bruce Quande was photographed on May 24,1963 flopping backward over the crossbar.
sentence_translations.translation: 但也许更令人惊讶的是，一名叫布鲁斯·匡德的高中生在1963年5月24日被拍到向后越过横杆。

sentence_translations.sentence: This was the same month that Fosbury recalls having flopped for the first time in the competition when he was at high school!
sentence_translations.translation: 这正是福斯伯里回忆自己在高中比赛中第一次使用背越式跳高的同一个月！

sentence_translations.sentence: But completing the Flop successfully was only half the battle; the return to earth still had to be negotiated.
sentence_translations.translation: 但是，成功完成背越式跳高只是成功了一半；返回地面这一环节仍需解决。

sentence_translations.sentence: Few would even consider such an experiment knowing they'd have to land on their necks.
sentence_translations.translation: 很少有人会考虑进行这样的尝试，因为他们知道自己将不得不以颈部着地。

sentence_translations.sentence: When Fosbury was jumping in high school, he had to land in pits which were filled with wood chips, sawdust, or sand.
sentence_translations.translation: 当福斯伯里在高中练习跳高时，他不得不落在装满木屑、锯末或沙子的坑里。

sentence_translations.sentence: On one occasion, Fosbury hit his head on the wooden border of the pit.
sentence_translations.translation: 有一次，福斯伯里的头撞在了坑的木制边框上。

sentence_translations.sentence: Another time he landed totally out of the pit, flat on his back, knocking the wind out of him.
